key_insight: Raising the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio densified Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings, cutting porosity and roughness while improving adhesion, with peak microhardness at an intermediate ratio.
engineering_relevance: Tuning the O2/C2H2 ratio offers a practical process-control lever to optimize coating quality for wear- and corrosion-resistant surface engineering on stainless steel components.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si coatings onto AISI 321 stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied the oxygen-to-acetylene ratio at 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 and monitored spraying with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: At O2/C2H2 = 1.2, porosity dropped to 0.90 ± 0.09% and roughness to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, while adhesion rose to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa; maximum microhardness was 1051.7 HV at 1.1.
watch_item: The abstract reports only three gas ratios, so the optimal setting may depend on torch dynamics, feedstock condition, and substrate preparation beyond the tested range.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
